transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I've been having a hard time lately with... this scar on my wrist. I mean, logically, I know it's probably not as bad as it looks to me. But whenever I'm out doing things, like when I'm at church or sitting down for bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone's eyes go right to it. It just feels like it's the very first thing they notice about me now, and it's really been bothering me.
When you are feeling this way about the scar, do you find yourself doing anything specific to try to check it, hide it, or seek reassurance about it?

Yes, I suppose I do. Before I leave the house, I’ll usually check my wrist in the hall mirror a few times just to see how it looks. I'll try pulling down my sleeves, or maybe I'll put on a bracelet to see if that covers it up better. And I do ask my husband sometimes if it looks obvious. He always says it’s barely there, but... I just feel the need to make sure.

Do you find yourself performing these checks or hiding behaviors because you are worried that something bad will happen if you don't, or is it specifically because you are unhappy with how the scar looks?

Oh, no, it's not because I think something bad is going to happen. I'm not worried about... well, a disaster or anything like that. It's really just because I'm unhappy with how it looks. I just feel self-conscious about the scar being visible, so I want to make sure it's covered up. That's really all it is.
Has this concern about your scar caused you to avoid social situations or interfered with your daily activities?

Yes, I suppose it has. I do some bookkeeping work, and... well, I’ve actually been late turning in some of my work lately. I just get so caught up trying to make sure my wrist won’t be noticed that I lose track of time or just can't focus on the numbers. 

And it's affected my social activities, too. I volunteer with a choir and a local theater group, and I’ve actually skipped a few of those commitments recently. Sometimes I just spend so much time trying to hide the scar before I leave the house that I end up just staying home instead.

When your husband or others tell you that the scar is barely noticeable, do you feel like they are just trying to be nice, or do you genuinely believe they simply cannot see the defect as clearly as you do?

I think... well, I think they just don't see it the way I do. My husband is a kind man, so maybe part of it is him trying to make me feel better, but mostly I genuinely believe he just doesn't notice it. To me, it feels so obvious, like it's the first thing anyone would look at. But when he looks at it, or if anyone else happens to mention it, they act like it's nothing. I just don't understand how they can't see how bad it looks.
Have you ever sought out a dermatologist, plastic surgeon, or any other professional to discuss ways to have the scar removed or altered?

No, I haven't actually. I haven't looked into seeing a dermatologist or a surgeon or anyone like that. I guess I've just been trying to deal with it on my own by keeping it covered up with my clothes and jewelry, so I haven't taken the step of talking to a professional about having it removed.

When you are checking your wrist in the mirror, do you find yourself performing any specific, repetitive actions, like tracing the scar or measuring it, or is it primarily just looking at it to see if it is visible?

I don't really measure it or trace it, no. It's mostly just looking to see if it's showing. Before I leave the house, I’ll usually stop and check my wrist in the hall mirror a few times. I'll... well, I'll try on a few different sleeves, or maybe put on a bracelet, just to see what covers it best. 

And I do sometimes ask my husband if it looks obvious. Even though he always says it’s barely there, I just feel like I need to check before I can go out.
Do you ever feel that because of this scar, your appearance is fundamentally flawed or ugly in a way that others might find unattractive?

No, I... I wouldn't say that. I don't think I'm ugly or, you know, fundamentally flawed. 

It's really just this one spot on my wrist that bothers me. I mean, I know the rest of me looks fine. I'm not worried about my whole appearance being ruined or that people find me completely unattractive overall. I just... I just really don't like the scar itself, and I'd rather people not look at it. But it doesn't make me feel like a hideous person or anything like that.

When you are in those social situations and you feel that people are looking at the scar, what specific emotions do you experience—do you feel mostly anxious, or is it more of a sense of shame or embarrassment?

I guess it's mostly embarrassment. I wouldn't say I feel super anxious or anything, it's just... well, it's embarrassing to think they might be staring at it. I just want to pull my sleeve down and hide it so they stop looking. It just makes me feel a bit self-conscious, but it's not like a deep shame or panic. Just uncomfortable.
